section_title: Sensible next steps while you decide
intro: General education only — not a personal plan. A physiotherapist or GP can tailor advice for you.
bullets: For common back, neck, and similar aches: keep gently moving within what you can manage; long bed rest usually isn’t helpful.

Ease back into usual activity using short bouts if needed. Some discomfort can be OK; stop and get advice if pain sharply worsens, or you get new weakness, numbness, chest symptoms, or other red-flag signs.

Ice or heat is fine if it comforts you — protect your skin, and don’t treat it as a cure. For recent soft-tissue injuries, follow clinician or Healthify soft-tissue advice (PEACE & LOVE), not prolonged icing as the main plan.

If this started after an accident or injury in New Zealand, ACC may be relevant — see the trusted ACC link. ACC does not cover every gradual or illness-related problem (for example, many osteoarthritis presentations).
optional_fifth_if_space: Scans are often unnecessary for common back pain without red flags — ask a clinician before chasing imaging.
